name: citor
baseline: oneTBB, Taskflow, OpenMP, dispenso, libfork, TooManyCooks
workload: Header-only C++20 pool with Chase-Lev forkJoin and parallelFor/Reduce/Scan; bundled parallel_bench covers dispatch latency, fan-out, reduce, scan, forkJoin vs ten peer pools; also in tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks recursive fork-join suite.
claimed_speedup: README: on single-CCD Zen 5 'citor wins the vast majority of contested bench cells'; runtime-benchmarks 64-core EPYC 7742: mean ratio to best 1.06x vs libfork 1.18x, TooManyCooks 1.32x, tbb 3.25x, taskflow 3.34x; skynet 24932 us vs tbb 142887 us, taskflow 185019 us; fib(39) 49966 us vs tbb 215592 us, taskflow 156590 us
compiler_and_flags: runtime-benchmarks: Clang 21.1.7 Release -O3 -march=native, tcmalloc; own CI GCC 14 / Clang 19, C++20
hardware: runtime-benchmarks: EPYC 7742 64 cores no SMT, Debian 13; own bench: Zen 5 9950X3D single CCD pinned, governor=performance, boost off; also AWS c7a.metal-48xl and c7i.metal-24xl
tradeoffs: Tuned for single-CCD Zen with physical-core pinning; header-only C++20.
caveats: Own README admits lower win-rate on multi-CCD and Intel mesh hosts; loses to OpenMP on barrier-bound stencils, to oneTBB on heavy-tailed reductions, to libfork on recursive fork-join with a multi-CCD pool; matmul and nqueens are slower than libfork/TMC in the summary table. Numbers are first-party-run (runtime-benchmarks is by the TooManyCooks author), but code, flags and CPU are public.
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'fast work stealing thread pool C++ benchmark faster than Taskflow oneTBB github'; numbers from runtime-benchmarks README

name: TooManyCooks
workload: Recursive fork-join coroutine benchmarks (skynet 100M tasks, nqueens, fib(39), matmul 2048) on 64 cores in tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks.
claimed_speedup: skynet 37949 us vs tbb 142887 us and taskflow 185019 us; nqueens 70248 us vs tbb 125730 us, taskflow 114721 us; fib(39) 86731 us vs tbb 215592 us, taskflow 156590 us; mean ratio to best 1.32x vs tbb 3.25x, taskflow 3.34x (derived tbb ~2.5x slower from page data)
hardware: EPYC 7742 64 cores no SMT, Debian 13, boost enabled, schedutil governor
tradeoffs: Requires C++20 coroutines, Clang 17+ or GCC 14+ (no MSVC); hwloc dependency; coroutine API rather than drop-in pool.
caveats: Benchmark suite is by the library's own author (first-party-run, but public code and flags). Fork-join workloads only; libfork is faster on nqueens and citor on skynet/fib. TooManyCooks repo is already in the catalog under a lowercase id, so this may fold as duplicate.
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'TooManyCooks C++20 coroutine thread pool benchmark vs libfork oneTBB taskflow'

name: ForkUnion
workload: N-body dispatch latency at N=512 and connected-components label propagation (84 fork-join rounds, ~27M edges) on four machines, same bit-identical workload across C++ and Rust.
claimed_speedup: README: ~3-6x faster than OpenMP and ~12-16x faster than Rayon and Taskflow on one parallel-for dispatch; 128-core Intel SPR N-body static/dynamic us: ForkUnion C++ 54/86 vs OpenMP 115/226, Rayon 483/739, Taskflow 666/694; connected components GTEPS: ForkUnion 46.5/20.9 vs OpenMP 28.2/0.4, Rayon 8.5/6.5, Taskflow 25.1/0.5
hardware: 18-core Apple M5 Pro, 24-core Intel RPL (Windows), 128-core Intel SPR, 192-core AWS Graviton 5
tradeoffs: Fork-join parallel-for pool only: no task graphs, no nested parallelism, no exceptions, no futures; C++17/C99/Rust/Zig APIs.
caveats: Not a general work-stealing pool; it deliberately avoids stealing for static/fetch_add claiming. Benchmarks are first-party and dispatch-bound by design; exact compiler versions not stated in the numbers section. Author blog 'Beyond OpenMP in C++ & Rust' not fetchable (blocked); numbers taken from the repo README.
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'Rust fork-join library faster than rayon join benchmark' surfaced ashvardanian.com 'Beyond OpenMP in C++ & Rust: Taskflow, Rayon, Fork Union'

name: scheduling (dpuyda)
workload: Recursive Fibonacci n=35, linear chain of 33.5M tasks and 2048x2048 matmul task graphs, vs Taskflow.
claimed_speedup: fib(35) 1661 ms vs Taskflow 15058 ms (derived ~9x from page data); linear chain 4158 ms vs 9951 ms; matmul 4134 ms vs 3970 ms (slightly slower)
tradeoffs: Under 1000 lines; Chase-Lev deque; C++20; borrowed code from Taskflow and Google Filament.
caveats: Baseline Taskflow is not in the category baseline list (TBB/OpenMP/Rayon). Paper is arXiv preprint (blocked here, not opened) so tier B is not confirmed; compiler flags not found on the page, so tier should be C if peer review is not verified. Matmul is on par or slower.
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'A simple and fast C++ thread pool implementation capable of running task graphs github'

name: chili
workload: Summing a balanced binary tree via fork-join at 1023 to 134M nodes.
claimed_speedup: Ryzen 7 4800HS 8 cores: 1023 nodes 3.4 us vs Rayon 51.1 us; 16.7M nodes 13.6 ms vs 58.1 ms; 134M nodes 101.8 ms vs 497.2 ms. Apple M1: 1023 nodes 3.5 us vs 29.2 us; 67.1M nodes 44.3 ms vs 167.1 ms
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 4800HS (8 cores), Apple M1 (8 cores)
tradeoffs: Heartbeat scheduling, join-only API; no parallel iterators or scopes.
caveats: Single synthetic tree-sum benchmark; flags and compiler not stated; Rust port of Spice. Found via HN thread 'Show HN: Chili' title only (thread blocked).
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'Rust fork-join library faster than rayon join benchmark chili spice forte' (Show HN: Chili. Rust port of Spice)

name: Spice
workload: Binary tree sum at 100M and 1000 nodes against an equivalent Rayon program.
claimed_speedup: Rayon adds ~15 ns per node overhead (7.48 ns to 22.99 ns); Rayon 1000-node case degrades up to ~60x slower at 32 threads while Spice avoids threading; Spice ~11x speedup at 16 threads (README, charts as SVG)
tradeoffs: Heartbeat scheduling, Zig only; about 500 lines, no tests; no slice/array support.
caveats: Zig library, not callable from C++ directly. Single benchmark; hardware and flags not stated in the text I read; Spice is slower than Rayon at 16 threads on the 100M case per its own README (11x vs 14x speedup), the claim is lower overhead. Author says no further development planned.
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'Rust fork-join library faster than rayon join benchmark chili spice forte'

name: Weave
workload: Overhead-bound task-parallel benchmarks (fibonacci, nqueens, DFS, BPC, SPC, heat, matmul) and data-parallel loops.
claimed_speedup: 'as low as 3x to 10x less overhead than Intel TBB and GCC OpenMP on overhead-bound benchmarks' (README, no table opened)
tradeoffs: Nim runtime (C/C++ backend); message-passing work-requesting instead of shared deques; needs to be called from Nim; only partially formally verified.
caveats: Quantitative per-benchmark numbers are in the benchmarks folder and the FOSDEM 2020 slides (blocked); I only recorded the README headline claim. Not usable directly from C++.
found_via: Blogs/talks: WebSearch 'Weave Nim multithreading runtime beats OpenMP TBB Cilk work-stealing benchmarks' (FOSDEM 2020 talk 'Designing an ultra low-overhead multithreading runtime for Nim')
